headline: 5-1 victory: Sweden smash Tunisia in World Cup opener
summary: Yasin Ayari scored twice as Sweden dominated their Group F debut, marking their highest World Cup score since 1938.
details: Sweden cruised to a dominant 5-1 victory over Tunisia in their World Cup Group F opener on Sunday. Yasin Ayari led the charge with two sensational goals, while Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres also found the net.
The win marks the first time Sweden has scored five goals in a single World Cup match since 1938, when they defeated Cuba 8-0. The team entered the tournament after a difficult qualifying campaign.
Ayari opened the scoring in the seventh minute after capitalizing on a goalkeeper error. Tunisia managed to pull one back before halftime through a glancing header by defender Omar Rekik.

Sweden regained control in the second half, with Isak assisting Gyokeres for the third goal on the hour mark. Substitute Mattias Svanberg added a fourth in the 84th minute after a VAR review confirmed the goal.
Ayari capped off the performance in stoppage time with a thunderous strike from outside the box. The result puts Sweden at the top of Group F with three points, ahead of Japan and the Netherlands.
caption:
Sweden just scored five goals in a single World Cup match for the first time since 1938!

Sweden cruised to a dominant 5-1 victory over Tunisia in their World Cup Group F opener on Sunday. Yasin Ayari led the charge with two sensational goals, while Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres also found the net.

The win marks the first time Sweden has scored five goals in a single World Cup match since 1938, when they defeated Cuba 8-0. The team entered the tournament after a difficult qualifying campaign.

Ayari opened the scoring in the seventh minute after capitalizing on a goalkeeper error. Tunisia managed to pull one back before halftime through a glancing header by defender Omar Rekik.

Sweden regained control in the second half, with Isak assisting Gyokeres for the third goal on the hour mark. Substitute Mattias Svanberg added a fourth in the 84th minute after a VAR review confirmed the goal.

Ayari capped off the performance in stoppage time with a thunderous strike from outside the box. The result puts Sweden at the top of Group F with three points, ahead of Japan and the Netherlands.

headline: GPS to be mandatory for all public transport in Bangladesh
summary: The government is introducing mandatory GPS tracking for all public transport vehicles to improve safety and monitoring.
details: The government has decided to make GPS tracking mandatory for all public transport vehicles across the country.
This move is aimed at enhancing the safety of passengers and allowing authorities to monitor vehicle movements in real-time.
The initiative is expected to help in reducing accidents and improving the overall management of public transportation systems.
Authorities will be implementing this requirement to ensure better tracking and accountability for transport operators.
